name: ECDF Plot
description: A step line showing, for every value, the share of observations at or below it. Every data point is shown and there are no bins to choose.
data_required: One continuous numerical column, optionally split by a categorical column.
use_when: Comparing whole distributions between groups, reading off percentiles (for example 'what share of orders are under $50?').
limitations: Less familiar to general audiences than a histogram.

name: Q-Q Plot
description: Plots the quantiles of your data against the quantiles of a normal distribution. Points on the diagonal mean the data is close to normal.
use_when: Checking whether a model assumption of normality holds, or spotting heavy tails and skew.
limitations: Only compares against one reference distribution at a time.

name: Histogram Grid
description: One small histogram for every numeric column, side by side, so the shape of each column can be compared at a glance.
use_when: The first look at a new table: spotting skew, caps (a spike at the maximum), gaps and odd values in every column at once.
limitations: Each panel has its own axis range, so heights are not comparable between panels.

name: 100% Stacked Bar Chart
description: A stacked bar where every bar is scaled to 100%, so you compare the share of each subcategory rather than totals.
data_required: Two categorical columns, optionally a numerical value to sum.
use_when: Comparing proportions across groups, for example the share of each product type per region.
limitations: Hides the absolute totals. Middle segments have no common baseline.

name: Dot Plot (Cleveland)
description: One dot per category placed at its value on a common scale. Uses less ink than a bar chart and does not need a zero baseline.
data_required: One categorical column and one numerical value (or an aggregate of it).
use_when: Ranking or comparing many categories, especially when values are far from zero.
limitations: Less familiar than bars for some audiences.

name: Lollipop Chart
description: A bar chart where each bar is replaced by a thin line ending in a dot. Easier to read when there are many similar-length bars.
data_required: One categorical column and one numerical value.
limitations: The dot centre is the value, which can be misread when dots are large.

name: Dumbbell Chart
description: Two dots per category joined by a line, showing the gap between two values such as before and after.
data_required: One categorical column and two numerical columns measured on the same scale.
use_when: Showing change or difference between two measurements per group.
limitations: Only works for exactly two values per category.

name: Heatmap (Cross-tab)
description: A grid where each cell is coloured by a value, such as the count of rows for each pair of categories.
data_required: Two categorical columns, optionally a numerical value to aggregate.
use_when: Finding which combinations of two categories are common or have high values.
limitations: Colour is less precise than position; label every cell when exact values matter.

name: Correlation Heatmap
description: A square grid showing the correlation between every pair of numerical columns, coloured from -1 (opposite) to +1 (move together).
use_when: Getting a quick overview of which variables move together before modelling.
limitations: Pearson correlation only captures straight-line relationships.

name: Hexbin Plot
description: A scatterplot for big data: the plane is cut into hexagons and each is coloured by how many points fall in it.
data_required: Two numerical columns, usually with thousands of rows.
use_when: A scatterplot would be an unreadable blob because of overplotting.
limitations: Individual outliers become hard to see.

name: Scatter Matrix
description: A grid of scatterplots, one for every pair of numerical columns, with histograms on the diagonal.
use_when: Exploring all pairwise relationships at once.
limitations: Becomes unreadable beyond about six columns.

name: Word Frequency Bar
description: A horizontal bar chart of the most common words in a text column, with common filler words removed.
use_when: A more accurate alternative to a word cloud when you need to compare frequencies.
limitations: Ignores meaning and context; 'not good' counts as 'good'.

name: Missing Values Map
description: A grid of rows by columns where missing cells are highlighted, with the percentage missing per column.
use_when: Before cleaning: seeing which columns have gaps and whether gaps happen in the same rows.
limitations: Large tables are sampled to keep the picture readable.
